Senses.PreferredTarget: at the gates of the six faculties
AlternateTargets: at the gateways of the six faculties
Senses.Explanation: Literally, "at the gate-heads" or "gateways" (門頭) of the "six faculties" (六根): eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. The phrase occurs 116 times in 84 allowlisted texts. Zhongfeng says, "there is a phrase at the staff-head, beneath the straw sandals, three thousand miles away, and at the gates of the six faculties; if recognized at the gates of the six faculties, there is no need to seek separately three thousand miles away" (有一句子在六根門頭，向六根門頭薦得). Yuanwu describes the six faculty-gates as "clean-naked and bare" and then says the audience will not "turn the light around and look back" (六根門頭淨裸裸赤灑灑，只是不肯回光返照). Huangbo's record speaks of scraping and clearing at the gates of the six faculties until not a hair of greed or craving remains untreated (於六根門頭刮削併當，貪愛有纖毫治不去). Later addresses say a "natural ancient buddha" constantly "shines light and shakes the earth at the gates of the six faculties" (六根門頭放光動地), while Ying'an describes them simply as "bare" throughout the twelve double-hours. These are observable predicates and locations assigned by the texts; the entry does not substitute a general theory of sensation.
Senses.Note: Counted collocations: "shine light and shake the earth at the gates of the six faculties" (六根門頭放光動地), 14; "clean-naked at the gates" (六根門頭淨裸裸), 1; "scrape clean at the gates" (六根門頭刮削), 4; "recognize at the gates of the six faculties" (向六根門頭薦得), 1. No direct dictionary-style self-definition was found; the stable locative construction and its predicates define the deployment.
